title: Housing and homelessness funding and after-hours service plan
subtitle: Waterloo Park Circuit contract, recruitment policy, election review, business plans, and a proposed King Street North development.
overview: Council approved $130,000 from its Community Priority and Contingency Reserve to support housing and homelessness work through 2023 {{vote:m6}}. It also accepted recommended steps toward a centralized after-hours call centre and a digital-first approach to customer service, with staff to report back on funding by the second quarter of 2023 {{vote:m4}}. No funding was approved for the call centre at this stage.

Council awarded the contract for Phase 1 of the Waterloo Park Circuit {{vote:m2}} and approved an updated recruitment policy {{vote:m3}}. It received a staff overview of the 2022 municipal election as information {{vote:m5}}. Councillors also heard 2023 business plans from the library, the CAO's office and Corporate Services, and a presentation from THEMUSEUM.

An informal public meeting was held on a proposal for a large mixed-use development at 475-485 King Street North. No decision was made. Staff will review the comments, including questions about traffic, flooding and land-use compatibility, and report back at a later formal meeting.
Council met in closed session earlier in the day. The minutes record the subjects only and report no outcome.

decisions.detail: Council approved report CAO2023-007 and $130,000 from the Community Priority and Contingency Reserve to support housing and homelessness work throughout 2023.

Council approved report IPPW2023-004, directed staff to report back by the second quarter of 2023 on funding options and next steps, and directed that the consultant's final report be posted online by February 1, 2023 and the staff report be sent to the Province.

Council awarded RFT 22-27 to 39 Seven Inc. for a total of $2,660,244.47 including unrecoverable HST, released $559,000 of 2023 capital funding, and approved $80,000 in project transfers for a bike shelter.
Council approved the H-012 Recruitment Policy and directed the Chief Administrative Officer and Director of Human Resources to update it as required.
Council received staff report CORP2023-002 on the 2022 election as information.

debate: On the after-hours call centre, the consultant argued that a digital-first approach and one central number would make service more consistent and free staff for complex requests. One councillor said they prefer speaking to a person and asked how people would reach one. The consultant said channels would not be eliminated, and that tickets with reference numbers would let residents track follow-up.

In the election discussion, a delegate from a local business organization argued that the regional sign by-law favours incumbents and hurts awareness. The delegate also urged a common voting system across the region and a task force to pursue it. The clerk said staff did not see signs as a turnout factor, noting that a region allowing signs had a larger drop. Online voting will be studied and brought back with pros and cons.

On housing and homelessness, staff described the funding as a starting point, including money for park and security patrols. Staff said the patrols are about connecting people to services rather than enforcement. Councillors asked about a public information page, student homelessness, and how businesses in uptown are supported. Staff said the page is under development.

On the King Street North proposal, councillors asked for a peer review of the land-use compatibility work, and raised air quality and noise near the highway, flood protection, and traffic at the Weber Street access. They also asked for a neighbourhood meeting on transportation. A resident speaking for nearby neighbours raised cut-through traffic and asked why extra height was needed.

During business plan questions, councillors asked about the interpretation-services pilot, funding for arts organizations, and fleet electrification. Staff said most of the fleet has no viable zero-emission option, and that trade agreements limit local-preference purchasing on larger contracts.
